steps.title: Brunello di Montalcino
steps.body: Montalcino, a hill town about 40 km south of Siena, is warmer and drier than Chianti. Brunello di Montalcino, DOCG since 1980, must be 100% Sangiovese, aged at least five years, two in oak; Riserva six years. The Biondi-Santi family created it in the late 19th century. Rosso di Montalcino is a younger, lighter version.

steps.title: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano
steps.body: Montepulciano, east of Montalcino, makes Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG from at least 70% Sangiovese, here called Prugnolo Gentile, aged at least two years. It's often softer than Brunello and more structured than Chianti. Since 2021, Pieve, a top tier from defined sub-areas, has been introduced.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its rule.
steps.explanation: Each Tuscan red has its own rules.

steps.body: Don't confuse Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, a Tuscan Sangiovese, with Montepulciano d'Abruzzo, a different grape from another region.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Brunello is 100% Sangiovese, aged five years
Vino Nobile is at least 70% Prugnolo Gentile
Montalcino is warmer and drier than Chianti
